headline: Nutanix sinks 15% after beating its targets and announcing that its chief executive will step down
summary: Nutanix fell 15.2% to $46.30 after reporting first-quarter revenue up 15% to $772 million and a record 32.1% adjusted operating margin, alongside the news that the board has begun searching for a successor to chief executive Rajiv Ramaswami.
why: The quarter itself beat every metric the company had guided: annual recurring revenue grew 15% to $2.63 billion, free cash flow rose to $209 million and adjusted EPS was $0.73. Nutanix guided second-quarter revenue of $820–830 million and full-year revenue of $3.18–3.23 billion, with free cash flow of $875–975 million.

The surprise was the leadership change. In a separate release the board said it had hired a search firm to find the next chief executive, with Ramaswami staying until a successor is in place. Unplanned CEO searches add uncertainty for a company that has cut guidance twice in the past year because of server shortages, and ARR growth slowing from 16% to 15% gave investors little reason to look past it.
